summary: Critiqued all 5 target claims side by side with their counter-claims. 3 original claims held up (2 gained confidence under adversarial testing: no faith-specific leader-first precedent, and defer campus-ministry coalitions; 1 held narrowly: diocese compliance sources are genuinely UK-context). 1 original claim was overstated and should be softened before the conclusion stage (relational-outperforms-digital campus-ministry claim, downgraded to a complementary/sequenced framing per Barna data). 1 counter-claim held up as a genuine, source-independent complication (EdTech champion-adoption's documented FERPA-trigger/pilot-trap failure mode strengthens, rather than replaces, the brief's existing doctrinal-safety risk caveat). No claim was found untraceable to its cited source and counter-evidence was substantive on every target claim, so no bounce was warranted.
